entries.text: They worked until midnight again and felt they had not done enough.
Session about rest. They noticed rest only feels allowed when they are ill.
Took Sunday morning off. Read in bed. Told themselves rest is part of the work.
Slow day, low energy. Instead of pushing, they said something kind to themselves and went to bed early.
Another evening with nothing to earn. It felt easier.
Very hard week at work, but they kept the Sunday morning rest anyway.

entries.text: Grey week. They felt heavy and stayed in bed most of Saturday.
They told Orca that sadness feels like failing. They noticed they hide it from friends.
Told a friend they were having a sad week. The friend came over with soup.
Sad morning. They opened the window, made tea and let it be a slow day without judging it.
They told their partner I am sad today, no reason. Got a hug.
Heavy day again. Went for a short walk anyway.

paths.name: Making room for sadness
paths.focus: about sad days and what helps

skills.name: Naming sadness
skills.in_your_words: You notice when sadness shows up, even when it does not seem to have a reason. You are also starting to spot the way it can feel like failing.

skills.name: Telling someone you are sad
skills.in_your_words: You can tell a friend you are having a sad week instead of keeping it all inside. You also notice that you often hide sadness from friends.

skills.name: Letting a slow day be
skills.in_your_words: You can make tea, open the window, and let it be a slow day without judging it. This is a gentle way you make room for sadness when the day feels heavy.

skills.name: Going for a short walk
skills.in_your_words: You go for a short walk anyway, even on a sad day. It is a small way to move through the day without waiting to feel different.
